# Password reset: architecture

<!-- Generated by `war` from records (projection `architecture`); edit the records, not this file. -->

How this is built, and why. Each decision lists the alternatives it was chosen over and what follows from it; requirements are named by id (the PRD states them). Every statement below is a record.

## Decisions

### DEC-pr1

Signed, stateless tokens with a server-side revocation list: expiry is
checked from the token itself, and a used or revoked token is refused by
the list.

*Constrains REQ-pr1.*

**Alternatives considered**

- **OPT-pr1.** Random opaque tokens stored server-side, looked up on every use.
- **OPT-pr2.** Signed tokens with no server-side state at all; a used token cannot be refused before it expires.

**Consequences**

- **CSQ-pr1.** Every confirm reads the revocation list, so the list is on the reset path and must be available whenever resets are. An entry can be dropped once the token it revokes has expired.

## Interfaces

What the parts expose to each other and to users.

| ID | Interface | Implements | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| IF-pr1 | `POST /password-reset` with an email address. Always answers 202, whether or not an account has that address, and emails a link carrying a token. | REQ-pr1 | — |
| IF-pr2 | `POST /password-reset/confirm` with the token and a new password. Answers 204 when the password is changed, and 410 for a token that is expired, already used or revoked. | REQ-pr1 | IF-pr1 |

## Constraints

- **CON-pr1.** Tokens are single-use and stored hashed. *Constrains REQ-pr1.*

## Outcomes

What a user can do once this ships.

> A user who forgot their password regains access without support.
>
> — OUT-pr1

## Requirements

What the work must do. Each says which outcome it serves.

- **REQ-pr1.** A reset token expires 15 minutes after issue. *Implements OUT-pr1; constrained by CON-pr1.*

## Constraints

What holds every solution in, whichever is chosen.

- **CON-pr1.** Tokens are single-use and stored hashed. *Constrains REQ-pr1.*

## Non-goals

What this work deliberately does not do.

- **NG-pr1.** Recovering an account without access to its registered email address. Support-assisted recovery and security questions are separate work.
- **NG-pr2.** Changing a password while signed in. That flow exists and does not change.

## Open questions

- **Q-pr1.** Should a completed reset sign the account out of its other sessions?
